title: How stable is a safety concept vector across a model's fine-tunes?

original_idea.body: Build a safety vector on a base model and measure transfer/cosine drift to 2-3 public fine-tunes, reporting a stability curve.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Concrete failure mode: safety vectors breaking after fine-tuning leaving models silently unmonitored; defensible chain.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Build a vector, apply across public fine-tunes, measure transfer + cosine drift; standard tools, beginner-feasible, zero training.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped: stability curve of a safety vector across 2-3 fine-tunes.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Public fine-tunes, no internal access; directly answers an open problem, externally doable, lab-deprioritized.

low_compute.reasoning: Inference-only across a few small models, no training; single GPU.

novelty.reasoning: Vector stability across fine-tunes is flagged as open but adjacent transfer/drift work exists; partly open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Stability across fine-tunes is an explicitly flagged open problem but adjacent transfer/drift studies exist; partly open.
